alate: Dorsum of head, thorax and abdomen blackish brown, antennae and wings brown, compound eyes purplish black, legs and sternites pale brown, the dorsum of each body segment densely covered with long and short pubescence. Head nearly round; fontanelle a narrow elongated slit, in profile depressed in the middle of its posterior margin; compound eyes oval and protruding, ocelli oval and slightly convex, the distance between ocellus and compound eye about equal to the diameter of the ocellus and greater than the distance from the compound eye to the lower margin of the head; postclypeus raised, the median suture distinct, about three times as wide as long. Antennae with 15 segments, the third short and small. Apical tooth of the left mandible almost as large as the first marginal tooth, the third marginal tooth short and small, the cutting edge between the marginal teeth slightly wavy. The T-shaped marking on the pronotum distinct, the anterior margin without a notch, the posterior margin slightly concave in the middle. Forewing: media arising independently at the wing-base suture, close to the cubitus, without branches behind it, cubitus with 10 to 11 branches; hindwing: media arising from the base of the radial sector, with two branches near the cubitus, cubitus with eight branches.
soldier: Head and antennae deep yellow, nasus brown. Head almost glabrous, the tip of the nasus with sparse soft hairs of unequal length; the anterior margin of the pronotum with only a few microchaetae. Head gourd-shaped, longer than wide, widest near the posterior end; distinctly narrowed behind the antennal sockets; the posterior margin of the head slightly concave inwards in the middle; in profile the nasus straight. Mandibles blunt, no pointed spine visible. Antennae with 13 segments, the fourth shortest, the third shorter than the second or nearly equal to it. Anterior part of the pronotum upturned, meeting the posterior part at about a right angle, neither the anterior nor the posterior margin with a median notch. Small soldier paler than the large soldier, the pilosity of the whole body very sparse; head also gourd-shaped, constricted behind the antennal sockets, widest at the occiput, the posterior margin shallowly incised in the middle; mandibles blunt and without a spine; antennae with 13 segments, the third short and small; neither the anterior nor the posterior margin of the pronotum concave in the middle.
